title: Bill under a tiered tariff
description: A tariff has tiers. The tier k covers the units above limits[k-1] (above 0 for the first tier) up to and including limits[k], and every unit in that tier costs rates[k]. The limits are the cumulative upper bounds of the tiers. The bill for a usage is the sum, over all tiers, of (units of the usage that fall in the tier) times the tier's rate; tiers above the usage add nothing. Return Ok with the bill. Check the input and return Err with exactly these messages, in this order, reporting the first one that applies: 'length mismatch' if the two lists differ in length; 'no tiers' if they are empty; 'bad limits' if the first limit is not above 0 or any limit is not above the one before it; 'bad rate' if any rate is negative; 'negative usage' if usage is below 0; 'usage above last tier' if usage is above the last limit.
notes: Precedence is tested with inputs that have two problems at once. A usage exactly on a limit stays in that tier; usage 0 bills 0. The tier width is limit minus previous limit, not the limit itself.
